To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the FEV/Pet1 gene is a transcriptional regulator of 5-HT neurons that is required for the maintenance of 5-HT neuronal phenotype in the adult, but not the embryonic, dorsal and median rapne nuclei.
the FEV gene is regulated by GATA factors, that FEV is expressed in a subset of 5-HT neurons that do not express Pet-1, and that FEV is not essential for 5-HT neuron survival.

we have determined the cis-regulatory elements that control expression of the human 5-HT neuron-specific ETS factor FEV, identified a GATA factor interaction that is critical for FEV transcription in 5-HT neurons and used FEV–LazZ transgenes to reveal the fate of Pet-1-deficient serotonergic precusors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of serotonin neuron development.
understanding the transcriptional mechanisms that control the development of serotonergic neurons in the mammalian brain.
how the human FEV gene is regulated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Pet-1 transcription factor plays a crucial role in the development of serotonin neurons.
the transcription factor Gata-2 binds to the FEV gene in the embryonic hindbrain and that this is required for serotogenic FEV expression.
the FEV/Pet 1 gene is an essential regulator of the 5-HT neuron gene expression program, and its transcription is controlled in part by direct interactions between GATA factors and FEV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FEV–Lacz transgene can be used to determine the fate of 5-HT neurons that lack Pet-1 expression.
the FEV gene is a direct transcriptional target of GATA-2, and that FEV expression is sufficient to direct transgene expression to the embryonic 5HT neuron precursors.
FEV expression is directly controlled by GATA factors and that FEV is required for normal 5-HT neuron distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Pet-1 gene is required for the development of the serotonin neurons of the brain, and the FEV-LacZ transgenic mouse is an important tool to investigate the fate of the Pet-1-deficient serotonin neurons.
FEV is a marker for the fate of 5-HT precursors in the adult dorsal and median raphee nuclei of Pet-1 mutant mice.
the transcription factor Gata-2 directly interacts with the Pet-1 promoter, which is important for Pet-1 expression in 5-HT neurons in the developing brain.
